label: BW-style / CLI-adapted

rubric_scores.evidence: Repeated columns, beams, purlins and windows establish a hall, but columns are unmodified eight-vertex boxes rather than flange-and-web I-sections. The roof is a plain slab, and hero junctions lack readable assembly detail.
Foreground conveyors, intermediate upright tank, rear elevated machinery and left window wall retain the broad reference organization. Principal equipment proportions are broadly plausible.
Several substantial housings and supported decks exist, but hero machine bodies read as flat pale gray rather than brushed satin stainless steel.
Yellow stairs and guarding are present, but continuous front rails cross the stair exits. The tank also obstructs the middle stair route, preventing coherent usable access.

Utilities consist of sparse smooth cylindrical segments and simple hanger rods. Required network density, readable reducers and wrinkled reflective foil are absent; several ends and hanger attachments are disconnected.

The upright vessel has formed heads, legs and plain nozzle cylinders, but no flange geometry. Its uniform bright green finish lacks the required worn dark-green character and shares the floor's roughness and metallic settings.

Substantial blue conveyor runs have rollers, supports and guides. However, the declared drive motor is only an unmodified cuboid without identifiable drive features or a readable transmission connection.

The green floor has specular reflections and systems remain color-separated. However, illumination reads as broad artificial fill rather than dominant side-window daylight, and stainless and foil lack differentiated surface responses.
The elevated diagonal hero viewpoint jointly shows the hall frame, foreground conveyors, tank, raised machines and overhead utilities with natural perspective and recognizable broad relationships.

The editable project opens, uses Cycles and AgX, and has no external image textures. Nevertheless, the original hero has conspicuous render noise; native Cycles denoising is disabled with only 16 samples.
The original final.png is a valid fully decoded PNG, but measures 512×267 instead of 3840×2160.

dimension_scores.evidence: The main industrial scene and color-coded equipment groups are recognizable, but equipment density and construction detail are substantially simplified.
Most large objects have supports, but the tank obstructs stairs, rails block landings, and utility connections and some machine supports are incomplete.
Yellow guarding, blue conveyors, green floor and tank preserve the principal palette; pale blocklike machinery and smooth ducts lose characteristic industrial silhouettes and finishes.
Primitive housings, faceted pipe bends, sparse fittings and conspicuous noise make the scene read as a preliminary model.
The principal foreground-to-background zoning is retained, but local clearances and access relationships are poorly resolved.
Machine, tank, railing and conveyor sizes broadly agree, while slender structural members and sparse equipment make the hall feel underdeveloped.
Floor reflections and soft illumination provide spatial cues, but daylight direction is weak and metallic systems lack distinct material character.
All broad object classes appear, but structural profiles, connections, utility density, flanges, functional drive detail and the required final-image resolution are missing.

same_model_bias_limit: Research and independent judge use Astra; separate sessions do not establish human independence.
